comparison: Perfect alignment on electrostatic potential analysis (C12, C103-C107, C143-C144). Both evaluations support these claims. Reviewer 1 explicitly praises the electric field distribution analysis and notes consistency with experimental results, matching OpenEval's assessment that the calculations provide a mechanistic explanation for voltage sensing.

Strong agreement on free energy calculations and gating charge contributions (C10-C11, C108-C111). Both evaluations support the quantitative agreement with experimental measurements. Reviewers explicitly affirm the gating charge predictions match experimental results, consistent with OpenEval's positive assessment.

Agreement on comparison with Cryo-EM structures (C9, C43, C86, C90-C91, C145-C146). Both evaluations support these claims. Reviewers acknowledge consistency with structural data and accept the authors' explanation for quantitative differences (absence of voltage), matching OpenEval's assessment.

Partial agreement on VSD-pore coupling mechanisms (C13, C126-C135, C140, C150-C152). OpenEval finds these claims supported by convergent analyses. Peer reviewers acknowledge the analyses as 'useful predictions' but express uncertainty due to incomplete opening and use of truncated channel, noting inferences may be 'only partially supported.'

Agreement on steered MD validation (C46-C48, C117-C122). Both evaluations support this approach. Reviewer 1 explicitly praises the steered MD simulations testing R213/R210 as primary gating charges, consistent with OpenEval's assessment that this provides orthogonal validation.

Agreement on main conclusions about non-domain-swapped topology (C49, C154-C156, C160). Both evaluations support these claims. Reviewer 2 explicitly endorses the 'helix-packing' mechanism conclusion for non-domain-swapped channels, and the editor notes the findings provide a solid basis for understanding this class of channels.

Agreement on core simulation methodology and VSD movements (C3, C5, C40-C42, C63). Both evaluations support the simulation approach. All three peer reviewers affirm the value and soundness of the methodology, with Reviewer 1 noting the prolonged timescale allows VSD equilibration, matching OpenEval's positive assessment.

Agreement on VSD movement observations (C6-C8, C83-C84, plus C56-C57, C60 from R4). Both evaluations support these findings. Reviewers explicitly support conclusions about limited VSD conformational changes compared to Kv channels and note the simultaneous movements of R210/R213 with S6.

Agreement on control simulations at 300 mV (C93, C148-C149). OpenEval views these as validating that movements are not artifacts. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this through describing methodology as 'sound' without raising concerns about high voltage use.

Divergent assessment of pore opening (C64-C68, C72). OpenEval finds these claims supported with appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, with Reviewer 1 noting timescale was 'likely insufficient to achieve a fully open state' and differences in replicate simulations suggest partial rather than complete opening.

Divergent assessment of conductance discrepancy (C74-C77). OpenEval finds the authors' explanations reasonable and the claims appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers express stronger uncertainty, with Reviewer 1 stating the order-of-magnitude underestimation suggests MD simulations may not yet provide insight into BK's large conductance mechanism.

Agreement on use of truncated channel construct (C70-C71, C162). Both evaluations support this as an appropriate design choice with acknowledged limitations. Reviewer 2 states authors provide 'strong rationale' for using truncated channel, matching OpenEval's assessment that limitations are appropriately acknowledged.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about voltage-gated ion channels (C1-C2, C15-C17) as well-supported by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background context.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about BK channel structure (C18-C26) as well-supported prior knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers did not assess these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims summarizing prior knowledge state (C27-C39) as appropriately supported and establishing the knowledge gap. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel contributions rather than literature review.

OpenEval evaluates Ca2+-bound open state analysis (C137-C139) as supported but somewhat speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these claims about Ca2+-driven activation pathway overlap.

OpenEval evaluates limitations and future directions (C161-C166) as appropriately stated. Peer reviewers touch on some limitations (C162 in R9) but do not provide comprehensive evaluation of all limitation statements and future work claims.
